lesson_body:
Welcome to Day 3 of Unit 4: Counting Base! Today, we will continue exploring the exciting world of numbers. Our focus will be on counting and understanding the significance of the numbers 1 through 20. We begin by reviewing what we learned yesterday about the number line and counting up to 20, using both visual aids and physical objects.

To make counting more exciting, we will play a fun game called ‘Count and Move!’ Students will be divided into small groups and given different colored counters. Each group will have a number chart from 1 to 20. As a teacher, I will call out a number, and each group will need to quickly find the corresponding number of counters and arrange them in a line. This will help reinforce one-to-one correspondence and the physicality of counting.

After the game, we will gather as a class to discuss our counting experiences. I will ask questions such as, ‘What was easy about counting today?’ and ‘How can we count beyond 20?’ This discussion helps to consolidate their learning and fosters critical thinking. We will use a large poster of a number line in the classroom to identify numbers that are more or fewer than a specified number. This will allow students to visually grasp the concept of number relationships.

Following our discussion, we'll engage in a storytelling exercise where I will read a fun counting book that features counting in everyday scenarios, like counting animals on a farm or counting fruits in a market. After the reading, I will ask students to brainstorm their own counting story ideas, which we will share in small groups, encouraging creativity in addition to math skills. 

To end our lesson, we will do a quick recap of today’s key points: Why we count, how we can use numbers in our daily lives, and how much fun counting can be! This is not just about numbers; it’s about exploring the world through them. We are getting ready to make our art project counting fun numbers in our surroundings, so stay tuned for tomorrow's activities!
interactive_assignment: For today’s hands-on activity, students will create ‘Counting Collages.’ Each student will receive a sheet of construction paper and a collection of magazines or printed images. Their task is to find pictures of items and count them out—such as animals, fruits, or toys—and then cut and paste those images onto their construction paper. Each collage should display a different number from 1 to 20, showcasing that number of items. After they create their collages, students will present their work to the class, explaining what they counted, how they found it, and why they chose those particular images. This will reinforce both counting skills and public speaking.

daily_assessment.question: How many apples are in the picture? Choose the correct number.
